turns.question_text: Your current planning app is simple, familiar, works offline, and handles your ordinary needs, but it cannot share reminders with other people. A new app adds shared reminders and better search, but moving everything would take about an hour and the new app is more complex. What would matter in deciding whether to switch?
turns.answer_text: The one deciding issue is whether I actually need shared reminders with another person. At present I don't, so I prefer the offline app.

turns.question_text: You promised to help a friend sort things for a move, but it is taking longer than expected and using up time you had set aside for yourself. Your friend is open to changing the arrangement. What would matter most in deciding what to do?
turns.answer_text: The commitment I made matters most, unless continuing would make me miss another promise. Those are the factors I'd use.

turns.question_text: You and a friend are planning a meal for just the two of you. You offer to organise and cook it, which will take several hours, and ask your friend to buy the ingredients. They say, “I'd like to do the meal, but paying for all the ingredients feels like too much for me.” What would you say next?
turns.answer_text: I'd suggest a smaller grocery bill. I normally want to make one alternative offer, but after that I'd rather drop the plan than keep negotiating.

turns.question_text: Your basic needs are covered, and you unexpectedly receive extra money equal to about one month of your ordinary living costs, with no debt, tax, or repayment obligation attached. What would you most want that money to do for you?
turns.answer_text: I'd want the money to take care of that particular matter I've had in mind. That's all I've said about what it would do.

turns.question_text: I'm spending several hours preparing supper for just myself and a friend. I proposed they cover the groceries; they say that cost is too much. What would I say back?
turns.answer_text: I'd suggest splitting the bill. Sometimes I want to keep negotiating and sometimes I want to abandon it straight away; I haven't said what my usual inclination is or what makes the difference.
